method: Per PR: a blind expert hunt from the diff and code; every candidate (the hunt, the AACR references with hand labels, and every comment any reviewer posted in our runs, anonymised) checked against the code, merged and graded, exclusions recorded; an adversarial critic per set spot-checked inclusions, exclusions and merges, and its 12 corrections were applied (2026-09-26). v2 (2026-09-26): the judge's 44 new-defect candidates from 12 judged runs were checked against the code — 1 added, 2 restated existing defects, 41 rejected (added to each PR's excluded list, which the judge now reads).

bitcoin__bitcoin@724546e.pr_summary: bitcoin-cli -netinfo now reports the node's local services. At level 0, which is the default, a new "Local services: network, bloom, witness, ..." line is printed before "Local addresses". It is built by the new ServicesList() helper, which lower-cases the names, turns '_' into spaces and joins them with ", ". At detail levels 1-4 the report header instead gets " - services <letters>", built with the existing FormatServices(). The PR touches one file, src/bitcoin-cli.cpp.

defects.title: std::string_view `services` dangles: it is bound to the temporary std::string from strprintf, then read on the next line
defects.statement: `services` is declared as `const std::string_view` and initialized from a conditional expression. Because strprintf returns std::string, the expression is a temporary std::string (the "" branch converts to std::string too), and that temporary is destroyed at the end of the declaration. The next statement passes the dangling view to strprintf to build the report header. On every `-netinfo 1..4` the header therefore reads freed memory: " - services nbwcl2" is too long for the small-string buffer, so this is a heap use-after-free that can garble the header, fail under ASan, or trigger clang -Wdangling-gsl. The fix is to own the string (`const std::string services{...}`).
defects.evidence: src/bitcoin-cli.cpp:585 at head: `const std::string_view services{DetailsRequested() ? strprintf(" - services %s", FormatServices(networkinfo["localservicesnames"])) : ""};` and :586: `std::string result{strprintf("%s client %s%s - server %i%s%s\n\n", CLIENT_NAME, FormatFullVersion(), ChainToString(), networkinfo["protocolversion"].getInt<int>(), networkinfo["subversion"].get_str(), services)};`. The ?: expression mixes std::string with const char[1], so its common type is a std::string prvalue, and the string_view is built through std::string::operator string_view. The temporary dies at the end of line 585's full-expression. How it is reached: NetinfoRequestHandler::ProcessReply runs on every `bitcoin-cli -netinfo N`. For N in 1..4, `DetailsRequested()` (line 407: `m_details_level > 0 && m_details_level < 5`) is true, so the heap-allocated string is created, destroyed, and then read at line 586. At level 0 the view also dangles, but its length is 0, so nothing is read.
defects.notes: To count, a comment must say that the string_view `services` at line 585 refers to a temporary std::string (the result of strprintf or the ternary) that is destroyed before line 586 uses it: a dangling view, use-after-free or UB. It counts with or without the fix `std::string services`. Near-misses that do not count: a generic remark that string_view is risky with no lifetime or temporary argument; a comment about FormatServices' output format; a comment that the level-0 empty-string branch is inefficient.

excluded.reason: Incorrect. The different formatting (lower-case words vs FormatServices' letters) is the intended level-0 output shown in the PR description. localservicesnames is always a server-built array of strings (rpc/net.cpp:687, GetServicesNames via serviceFlagsToStr), and the existing FormatServices already calls get_str() on it the same way, so the defensive-typing concern has no reachable path.

Incorrect. The order is not arbitrary: serviceFlagsToStr (protocol.cpp:108-118) walks the service bits in ascending order, so the output is deterministic and matches bit order and the letter order of FormatServices.
Incorrect. The project requires C++20 (CMakeLists.txt:68 `set(CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD 20)`, STANDARD_REQUIRED ON), and <algorithm> is already included, so std::ranges::replace cannot break the build.
These are requests to add functional-test coverage for the new output modes. Test requests are not defects.

This asks to update the `-netinfo help` level descriptions (the level-1 help still says "Like 0" although the new services line appears only at level 0). It is a documentation request about a human-readable dashboard whose help explicitly says the output "will change regularly". It has no functional consequence, so it is not a defect under this benchmark's rules.

FreeCAD__FreeCAD@699b45c.pr_summary: This PR cleans up MSVC warnings across 16 files, with 33 additions and 27 deletions. It adds float literals and casts where values narrow from double to float: View3DInventor(Viewer), ViewProviderPlane, DAGRectItem, Tools.h fromPercent, and three angle-wrap lines in SoDatumLabel. It changes printf-style specifiers: StackWalker %d becomes %ld for DWORD arguments, and pyarea on Windows goes from %Iu to %zu. It adds `case NumSymTypes` and `default: break` for enumerators the switches did not handle, drops unused catch variables and an unused lambda capture, and marks a debug-only local [[maybe_unused]]. FemVTKTools' countScaPos changes from int to size_t. PropertySheet::getLinksTo now passes std::string instead of .c_str() to the ObjectIdentifier ctor. The old const char* argument silently picked the (owner, bool localProperty) overload, so this is a latent fix, and the vector-identifier getLinksTo has no in-tree callers. Two test tweaks are included. Almost every hunk keeps behaviour the same. Two changes do not fully do what they intend. The SoDatumLabel angle wraps still multiply by a double literal, so the float += double narrowing remains. The StackWalker DWORD specifiers become the signed %ld instead of %lu.

defects.title: SoDatumLabel angle-wrap casts leave the right-hand side double, so the float += double narrowing (C4244) the PR targets remains
defects.statement: The PR rewrites `range += 2.0 * M_PI` and `endangle += 2. * M_PI` as `2.0 * static_cast<float>(M_PI)` and `2. * static_cast<float>(M_PI)`. Because `2.0` and `2.` are double literals, double * float still produces a double. Each compound assignment is still float += double with an implicit narrowing, so the MSVC C4244 warning this PR is meant to silence still fires in all three places. The cast only lowers the precision of the constant. The warning-free form is `2.0F * (float)M_PI`, which the same file already uses at line 1541.
defects.evidence: The head has `float range = endAngle - startAngle; if (range < 0.) { range += 2.0 * static_cast<float>(M_PI); }` at SoDatumLabel.cpp:82-84. At :552 and :695 it has `float endangle = atan2f(...); if (endangle < startangle) { endangle += 2. * static_cast<float>(M_PI); }`. Under the usual arithmetic conversions, a double literal times a float gives a double, so `float += double` still narrows. The file's correct form is at :1541, `endangle += 2.0F * (float)M_PI;`, and float-only forms appear at :1199/:1201 as `angle -= (float)M_PI;`. The code runs on every glDrawArc call with a negative range and on every arc/angle datum label render where endangle < startangle. The impact is a compile warning that stays, plus a sub-ulp change to the constant. There is no functional breakage.
defects.notes: To count, a comment must say that `2.0`/`2.` is a double literal, so the expression stays double. It must also say either that the double-to-float conversion/warning is not fixed, or that `2.0F`/`2.0f` is needed. Pointing at any of the three sites counts. Near-misses that do not count: comments only about float vs double performance with no mention that the narrowing or warning remains (the dataset framed it as 'performance'; accept that framing only if it says the arithmetic is still double); comments about the default argument `endAngle=2.0*M_PI` at :81, which the PR did not touch; and generic advice to prefer float literals elsewhere.

defects.title: StackWalker prints DWORD (unsigned long) arguments with the signed %ld specifier instead of %lu
defects.statement: The PR replaces `%d` with `%ld` in every StackWalker diagnostic format that takes DWORD arguments: module size and result, the file-version words v1..v4, entry.lineNumber, GetLastError `gle`, symOptions, and the OS-version fields. DWORD is `unsigned long`, so the matching specifier is `%lu`. As written, specifier and argument still disagree in signedness. Any value with the high bit set prints as a negative number, for example SYMOPT_DEBUG 0x80000000 in symOptions or an HRESULT-style GetLastError code. The PR's own goal of making specifiers match their types is therefore only half done.
defects.evidence: StackWalker.cpp:1455-1462 has `void StackWalker::OnLoadModule(..., DWORD size, DWORD result, ...)`, and :1473 formats them with `"... size: %ld (result: %ld) ..."`. At :1483-1486, `DWORD v4 = (DWORD)(fileVersion & 0xFFFF); ...` is printed with `"%ld.%ld.%ld.%ld"` at :1490. `entry.lineNumber` (DWORD) uses `%ld` at :1540. `OnDbgHelpErr(LPCSTR, DWORD gle, DWORD64)` uses `GetLastError: %ld` at :1559. `OnSymInit(LPCSTR, DWORD symOptions, ...)` uses `symOptions: %ld` at :1576. `ver.dwMajorVersion` and the other OS-version DWORDs use `%ld` at :1609. DWORD is typedef'd `unsigned long` on Windows, and `%ld` expects a signed `long`. This is not a regression, since the old `%d` was signed too. The impact is only cosmetic diagnostic output, and only for values >= 2^31.
defects.notes: To count, a comment must say that the new `%ld` is signed while the DWORD argument is unsigned (unsigned long), and that `%lu` or another unsigned conversion is the right specifier. Any one of the listed lines counts. Near-misses that do not count: claims that `%ld` is the wrong size, since long and DWORD are both 32-bit on Windows; comments about the `%p` or `0x%x` conversions; and comments about the `case NumSymTypes` addition.

excluded.reason: This is a style preference. `case NumSymTypes: break;` exists only to satisfy C4062. An assert(false) or a future std::unreachable in a crash-reporting path, where SymType comes from dbghelp at runtime, is not a needed fix, and adding one could be harmful.
The redundant `std::roundf` on an integral long predates the PR, which only added the cast. It is harmless and has no behavioural consequence. This is a nit.
The long-to-float precision concern is speculative. float is exact up to 2^24, and callers pass 0-100 percentages. The suggested double rewrite is equally redundant.

The premise is wrong or harmless. On Qt6 `QColor::setAlphaF` takes a float, so `0.15f` removes a double-to-float truncation, which is the PR's purpose. On Qt5 the float-to-double widening is lossless.
Making `nearClippingPlane` const is pure style. It is a local used once.
`nvertices` is std::size_t, so `%zu` is correct. The project requires C++20, which implies an MSVC with a UCRT that supports %zu (VS2015+). The 'older MSVC' concern does not apply.
This is generic advice to log exception details. The PR dropped an unused catch variable to fix a warning, and the existing message is adequate. Not a defect.

Returning the incoming dimType for every other geometry is the function's documented, pre-existing behaviour. The PR only made the fallthrough explicit with `default: break;`. Nothing is newly ignored.
Tools.h:148 redundant roundf. The redundancy predates the PR and has no consequence, so this is a simplification nit (same as ref 7).

pyarea.cpp: collapsing the three-way #if into a single %zu is a cleanup suggestion. The 32-bit `%d` branch's signedness mismatch predates the PR and was not touched. The PR's Windows change is correct.
DimensionValidators: the duplicated 2D/3D switch predates the PR. The PR only added identical `default: break;` arms to silence C4062, so asking to consolidate is a refactor request, not a defect.

This is not a defect. Passing std::string makes emplace_back select the intended (owner, property) ctor. The old const char* argument silently chose (owner, bool localProperty=true) and produced an empty identifier. The change fixes that, and the vector-identifier getLinksTo overloads have no in-tree callers, so no caller relied on the old behaviour.

This is correct. countScaPos is only compared against the size_t elements of scalarPos via std::find, and it is only reset to 0 or incremented. The uninitialised use when a -2 line precedes any -1 line predates the PR, which did not change it.

CherryHQ__cherry-studio@83a2594.pr_summary:
PR #5540 ("feat: 支持自定义助手地址") adds a custom assistant-list URL setting: a `settings.defaultaides` field (initial value 'settings.defaultaides', reducer `setefaultAides`), a new Data Settings panel (`DefaultaidesSettings.tsx` plus a menu entry with an inline star icon), and locale strings. The strings are nested `settings.data.default_aides.*` in zh-CN only; the other locales get a flat `settings.defaultaides`. `useSystemAgents` now reads the setting from `store.getState()` during render. If the value starts with 'http' it calls a new `useRemoteSystemAgents`, which waits 500 ms, fetches the URL and casts the JSON to Agent[]. Otherwise it calls the original local hook, now named `useLocalSystemAgents`, which reads the bundled agents.json.

Defects found:
- Hooks are called conditionally, which breaks the repo's rules-of-hooks lint, and CI runs that lint.
- The UI strings only resolve in zh-CN.
- The default value is a raw i18n key.
- A failed remote load does not fall back to the bundled agents.
- The remote payload is not validated.
- The source setting is read without subscribing to the store.
- Every mount pays the 500 ms delay and a re-fetch, with no caching.
- There is no persist migration.
- The exported action name is misspelled.

defects.title: useSystemAgents / useRemoteSystemAgents call hooks conditionally (rules-of-hooks violation): CI lint fails, and hook order differs between the local and remote sources
defects.statement: useSystemAgents returns `useLocalSystemAgents()` or `useRemoteSystemAgents()` from different `if` branches. The two hooks call different hook sequences: local calls useState, then useRuntime (a selector hook), then useEffect; remote calls useState, then useEffect. useRemoteSystemAgents also calls `useEffect` after an early `return agents`. The repo's ESLint config enables `reactHooks.configs['recommended-latest']`, where rules-of-hooks is an error that `--fix` cannot repair, so the PR CI `yarn lint` step fails. At runtime, a mounted consumer that re-renders after the setting crosses the http/non-http boundary would render a different hook sequence, which is React's hook-order error.
defects.evidence: index.ts:20-29 `const { defaultaides } = store.getState().settings; if (defaultaides === null || defaultaides === undefined) { ...; return useLocalSystemAgents(); } if (!defaultaides.startsWith('http')) { return useLocalSystemAgents(); } else { return useRemoteSystemAgents(); }`. index.ts:36-40 `if (defaultaides === null || defaultaides === undefined) { ... return agents; } useEffect(() => {` puts a hook after an early return. useLocalSystemAgents (61-63) calls useState, then `useRuntime()` (= `useAppSelector(...)`, useRuntime.ts:4-6), then useEffect; the remote hook calls only useState and useEffect. eslint.config.mjs:15 `reactHooks.configs['recommended-latest']` sets rules-of-hooks to error. The repo already has to opt out of this rule explicitly: useKnowledge.ts:1 `/* eslint-disable react-hooks/rules-of-hooks */`. pr-ci.yml:45-46 `- name: Lint Check / run: yarn lint`. package.json `"lint": "eslint . ... --fix"`: --fix cannot repair rules-of-hooks, so the step exits non-zero. Runtime reachability is narrow today, because both consumers (the AgentsPage route and the AddAssistantPopup modal) normally remount after a settings change. The lint break is the concrete consequence.
defects.notes: To count, a comment must say one of these: the local and remote hooks are selected/called conditionally; the two branches have different hook sequences, so hook order changes and React can throw a hook-order error; useEffect is called after an early return; or this violates the Rules of Hooks / fails react-hooks lint. These do NOT count on their own: saying only that store.getState() is non-reactive or should be useSelector (that is D6); saying only that the null check is duplicated or dead; generic 'refactor this hook'.

defects.title: New settings UI strings exist only in zh-CN; en-US (fallback), ja, ru, zh-TW and the machine-translated locales show raw i18n keys
defects.statement: The new menu entry and panel call t('settings.data.default_aides.title'), '...repo_url' and '...repo_url_placeholder'. Only zh-cn.json defines `settings.data.default_aides`. en-us, ja-jp, ru-ru and zh-tw instead add a flat, unused `settings.defaultaides` string at the wrong path under a different name. en-US is the fallbackLng, so every non-zh-CN user sees the literal key strings in the Data Settings menu, the section title, the row label and the placeholder. This contradicts the PR's claim that multi-language support was updated.
defects.evidence: DataSettings.tsx:116 `title: 'settings.data.default_aides.title'`, rendered at :180 `title={t(item.title || '')}`. DefaultaidesSettings.tsx:26/29/36 use `t('settings.data.default_aides.title' | '.repo_url' | '.repo_url_placeholder')`. Parsing the head JSON gives: en-us/ja-jp have `settings.defaultaides` = 'Built-in'/'内蔵' and no `settings.data.default_aides`; zh-cn has `settings.data.default_aides` = {repo_url, repo_url_placeholder, title} and no `settings.defaultaides`. i18n/index.ts:40 `fallbackLng: defaultLanguage`; packages/shared/config/constant.ts:164 `defaultLanguage = 'en-US'`. The translate/{el-gr,es-es,fr-fr,pt-pt}.json files are untouched, so they fall back to en-US, which also lacks the keys. No t('settings.defaultaides') call exists anywhere.
defects.notes: To count, a comment must say that the keys used by the new UI (`settings.data.default_aides.*`) are missing from the non-zh-CN locales, or that en/ja/ru/zh-TW define `defaultaides` at a different name/path, so users of those languages (and the en-US fallback) see raw keys or untranslated labels. Pointing at any one of the locale files or at the t() call sites is enough. Does NOT count: a comment that says zh-cn.json is the wrong one and should be renamed to 'defaultaides' (backwards). Also does NOT count: a pure casing or naming-style remark about 'default_aides' vs other keys with no mention of lookup failure.

defects.title: A failed remote load leaves the system assistant list empty; no fallback to the bundled agents despite the PR's 'fallback mechanism' claim
defects.statement: With an http URL configured, useRemoteSystemAgents starts from `[]`. Any failure (offline, non-2xx, invalid JSON) is caught and only console.error'd. The bundled resources/data/agents.json is never read. The Agents page and the Add Assistant popup then show no built-in assistants at all, and the user gets no indication why. The PR body advertises 'Add fallback mechanism for assistant loading', but the only fallback applies to non-http values.
defects.evidence: index.ts:33 `const [agents, setAgents] = useState<Agent[]>([]);`; :45-47 `if (!response.ok) { throw new Error(...) }`; :50-52 `} catch (error) { console.error("Failed to load agents:", error); }`; :58 `return agents;`. There is no call into the local loader or `_agents` on failure. Compare useLocalSystemAgents at :61-74, which reads `resourcesPath + '/data/agents.json'`. The PR body says: 'Add fallback mechanism for assistant loading'.
defects.notes: To count, a comment must say that when the remote fetch/parse fails, the built-in/bundled assistants are not used as a fallback and the system agent list stays empty. Does NOT count: a generic 'handle errors / show an error toast' comment that does not mention losing the bundled list; payload validation (D4); abort/cleanup requests.

defects.title: Remote JSON is cast to Agent[] without runtime validation; a wrongly shaped payload crashes the Agents page and the Add Assistant popup
defects.statement: `await response.json() as Agent[]` publishes whatever the user-configured URL returns. If it is a JSON object (for example a wrapped `{agents:[...]}` or an API response), AgentsPage's effect calls `groupByCategories(systemAgents)`, and `data.forEach` throws. AddAssistantPopup spreads `...systemAgents` inside useMemo during render, which throws on a non-iterable. Entries without `name`, or with a non-array `group`, throw in `agent.name.toLowerCase()` or `item.group?.forEach`. There is no error boundary around these consumers, so the renderer tree crashes. The bad URL is persisted, so the crash repeats every time the Agents page or the popup opens.
defects.evidence: index.ts:48-49 `const agentsData = await response.json() as Agent[]; setAgents(agentsData);`. AgentsPage.tsx:33 `const systemAgentsGroupList = groupByCategories(systemAgents)` leads to index.ts:79-80 `data.forEach((item) => { item.group?.forEach(`. AddAssistantPopup.tsx:38 `const allAgents = [...userAgents, ...systemAgents] as Agent[]`, and :40 `agent.name.toLowerCase()`. App.tsx has no top-level ErrorBoundary around the routes or TopView.
defects.notes: To count, a comment must say that the fetched remote JSON is trusted/cast as Agent[] without checking its shape, and that a non-array or malformed payload breaks the consumers (a crash in groupByCategories/forEach/spread/name access) or should be treated as a load error. Does NOT count: the no-fallback-on-failure point (D3); 'use a stricter type than any' on getAgentsFromSystemAgents (pre-existing).

defects.title: The new setting's initial value is the raw i18n key 'settings.defaultaides', shown verbatim in the URL input
defects.statement: initialState sets `defaultaides: 'settings.defaultaides'`: a translation key stored as the setting's value and never passed through t(). On a fresh install the Assistant URL input binds directly to it and displays the literal 'settings.defaultaides'. The 'Built-in' strings added to the locales are never rendered. The value means 'use built-in' only by accident, because it does not start with 'http'.
defects.evidence: settings.ts:210 `defaultaides: 'settings.defaultaides', // 默认智能体`. DefaultaidesSettings.tsx:16 `const Aides = useSelector((state: RootState) => state.settings.defaultaides)` and :33 `value={Aides || ''}`, with no t(). index.ts:25 `if (!defaultaides.startsWith('http')) { return useLocalSystemAgents(); }`.
defects.notes: To count, a comment must say that the default/initial value is an i18n key (or an internal-looking literal) instead of an empty/null/real value, and that it is shown to users in the input or only works because it is not http. Does NOT count: comments about the missing `settings.data.default_aides` translations (D2); a pure naming/casing remark on the field.

defects.title: useSystemAgents reads the source setting via store.getState() during render: consumers never subscribe to changes
defects.statement: The source selection reads `store.getState().settings.defaultaides` instead of subscribing via useSelector/useAppSelector. A change to the setting therefore never re-renders the hook's consumers, and a mounted consumer keeps the old source until something unrelated re-renders it. This is latent today, because the two current consumers remount after a settings visit. It bypasses react-redux and is exactly what makes the conditional hook dispatch (D1) look safe.
defects.evidence: index.ts:20 `const { defaultaides } = store.getState().settings` and :34 the same again inside useRemoteSystemAgents. The writer is DefaultaidesSettings.tsx:18-19 `dispatch(setefaultAides(e.target.value))`. Consumers are AgentsPage.tsx:29 and AddAssistantPopup.tsx:32. App.tsx routes have no keep-alive, so AgentsPage remounts on navigation, which keeps this latent today.
defects.notes: To count, a comment must say that store.getState() is a non-reactive snapshot, so consumers do not update/re-fetch when the URL setting changes, and should use useSelector/useAppSelector. Does NOT count: a comment that only flags the conditional hook calls or hook order (that is D1). A comment that makes both points counts for both.

defects.title: Remote agents are fetched on every mount after a hard-coded 500 ms sleep and are never cached
defects.statement: Unlike the local path, which caches in the module-level `_agents`, useRemoteSystemAgents starts from `[]`, sleeps 500 ms for no reason, and re-fetches the URL every time AgentsPage mounts or the Add Assistant popup opens. Each open costs at least 500 ms plus a network round-trip, during which the list holds only user agents and then jumps.
defects.evidence: index.ts:33 `useState<Agent[]>([])`; :43 `await new Promise(resolve => setTimeout(resolve, 500));`; :44 `await fetch(resourcesPath)`. Nothing writes `_agents`. Compare :67 `if (!resourcesPath || _agents.length > 0) return` in the local hook.
defects.notes: To count, a comment must say that the artificial 500 ms delay slows every load, or that the remote list is refetched on every mount with no caching (unlike the local `_agents` cache). Does NOT count: a comment that only asks for an AbortController/cleanup or warns about setState after unmount (in React 19 that is a no-op).

defects.title: No redux-persist migration for the new settings field: upgraded installs get undefined and log console.error on every render
defects.statement: The store persists `settings` with redux-persist's default level-1 merge, so a rehydrated settings object replaces initialState.settings. The repo adds each new settings field through a numbered migration in migrate.ts plus a version bump. This PR adds neither, so every existing install has `defaultaides === undefined`, outside its declared `string | null` type. useSystemAgents then logs `console.error('defaultaides is null or undefined')` on every render of AgentsPage and AddAssistantPopup, and existing users get a different default from new users ('' vs 'settings.defaultaides').
defects.evidence: store/index.ts:41-47 `persistReducer({ key: 'cherry-studio', storage, version: 96, blacklist: ['runtime', 'messages'], migrate }, rootReducer)` has no stateReconciler, so it uses the default autoMergeLevel1. migrate.ts has no entry setting `state.settings.defaultaides`; repo convention is shown by e.g. '94': `state.settings.enableQuickPanelTriggers = false`. index.ts:21-22 `if (defaultaides === null || defaultaides === undefined) { console.error('defaultaides is null or undefined');`.
defects.notes: To count, a comment must say that there is no migration/persist version bump for `defaultaides`, so existing users' persisted settings lack it (undefined), with any consequence such as the error log or an inconsistent default. Does NOT count: the raw-i18n-key default value (D5); the duplicated null check (ref 7).

defects.title: The exported Redux action is misspelled `setefaultAides`
defects.statement: The new reducer and exported action creator are named `setefaultAides`, missing the 'D' of Default. It becomes part of the settings slice's public API. Anyone searching for or importing `setDefaultAides` will not find it, and renaming it after merge means churn across consumers.
defects.evidence: settings.ts:459 `setefaultAides: (state, action: PayloadAction<string>) => {`; :576 `setefaultAides,` in the export list; DefaultaidesSettings.tsx:4 `import { setefaultAides } from '@renderer/store/settings'`.
defects.notes: To count, a comment must point out the `setefaultAides` typo (missing D) in the action/reducer name. Does NOT count: casing preferences for `defaultaides` / `DefaultaidesSettings` (taste, excluded).

excluded.reason: Backwards. zh-cn.json is the only locale that matches the keys the code uses (`settings.data.default_aides.*`). Renaming it to 'defaultaides' as proposed would break zh-CN too. The claim that the code uses 'defaultaides' is false.
`getAgentsFromSystemAgents(systemAgents: any)` is pre-existing code the PR does not touch, and the advice is generic typing. The repo also turns off @typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any.

Suggests extracting the small duplicated null guard into a helper, which is taste. The only concrete problem in that block is that useEffect is called after its early return, which is D1, and this ref does not identify it.

The repo is on React 19, which removed the setState-on-unmounted warning, so the stated consequence does not exist. A URL change while mounted is not reachable (consumers remount). A missing abort is at most a nit.
Identifier casing ('DefaultaidesSettings' vs 'DefaultAidesSettings') is naming taste with no behavioural impact.

The inner `AidesIcon` follows the file's existing JoplinIcon/SiyuanIcon pattern. The repo explicitly disables '@eslint-react/no-nested-component-definitions', and a static 16px SVG costs nothing measurable.
False premise. Underscore keys are already the norm in this menu (export_menu, markdown_export, divider_0), and 'default_aides' matches the i18n namespace.
`React.ChangeEvent` in a type position resolves through @types/react's UMD global namespace. The repo does this widely without importing React, so there is no TS error.
Blank-line formatting only.
Field-name casing (`defaultaides` vs `defaultAides`) is naming taste.

bluewave-labs__Checkmate@29e03a6.pr_summary: Adds a GitHub Actions workflow (.github/workflows/poeditor-sync.yml) that runs by hand or nightly, a Node script (.github/scripts/download-translations.js) and a README. For each requested language the script exports translations from POEditor (key_value_json by default, or json, which it converts from an array into a flat map) and writes temp/<lang>.json. The workflow checks each file is non-empty, valid JSON, copies it over src/locales/, commits, and pushes with GITHUB_TOKEN to the checked-out branch. The app (src/Utils/i18n.js) globs src/locales/*.json into i18next resources. It uses "gb" as the primary and fallback language, and every locale file becomes an entry in the LanguageSelector.

defects.title: Manual and scheduled runs use different English codes (en vs gb); one default path writes a stray en.json and leaves gb.json stale, the other asks POEditor for 'gb'
defects.statement: The workflow_dispatch input defaults to "tr,en", but the env fallback that applies on the nightly schedule is 'tr,gb'. The script's own default is 'tr,en' and the README says the default is tr and gb. The script writes temp/<code>.json verbatim and the workflow copies it into src/locales, while the app is keyed on "gb" (primaryLanguage and fallbackLng). So a default manual run adds a new en.json, which becomes an extra "EN" language in the selector with no flag, and never refreshes gb.json. The nightly run instead requests 'gb'. Whichever code the POEditor project uses, one of the two default triggers is wrong: it either syncs the wrong English file or fails the export and exits 1.
defects.evidence: poeditor-sync.yml:10 `default: "tr,en"` vs :60 `LANGUAGES: ${{ github.event.inputs.languages || 'tr,gb' }}`. The fallback applies only when the input is empty, which is always the case on schedule. download-translations.js:12 `(process.env.LANGUAGES || 'tr,en').split(',')`; :64 `path.join(process.cwd(), 'temp', `${language}.json`)`; workflow:83 `cp -r temp/* src/locales/`. README.md:25 says "the default languages `tr` and `gb`", and the PR body says "tr and en". App side: src/Utils/i18n.js:6 `const primaryLanguage = "gb";`, :8 `import.meta.glob("../locales/*.json")`, :24 `fallbackLng: primaryLanguage`. src/Components/LanguageSelector.jsx `Object.keys(i18n.options.resources)` and `fi fi-${lang}`. Existing locale files are gb.json and tr.json. Script:37-39 throws, and it exits 1 at :72-73, on a non-success export.
defects.notes: To count, a comment must point out the en-vs-gb language-code mismatch between any two of: the manual input default (tr,en), the scheduled fallback (tr,gb), the script default (tr,en) and the README (tr,gb). Stronger hits add the consequence: the app uses gb.json, so the manual default writes en.json and leaves gb stale, or the nightly run requests an unsupported code. A comment that only says the README contradicts the manual default counts, because it is the same inconsistency. Near-misses that do not count: generic advice to validate language input, or the whitespace-trimming issue (D5).

defects.title: key_value_json export is written unfiltered, so untranslated terms land in tr.json as "" and render blank instead of falling back to gb
defects.statement: The default key_value_json path saves POEditor's export exactly as received. The export request passes no filters or fallback_language, and POEditor includes untranslated terms with empty-string values. Today tr.json holds only the translated subset (105 lines vs 178 in gb.json), so missing Turkish keys fall back to gb. After a sync those keys become "", and i18next (24.x, returnEmptyString left at its default of true) treats an empty string as a valid translation, so Turkish users see blank labels. The array path does drop empty definitions; the default path does not.
defects.evidence: The export body is only `{api_token, id, language, type}` (script:29-35): no `filters: 'translated'` and no `fallback_language`. Script:50 `let formattedTranslations = translations;`. Only the `Array.isArray` branch (:53-60) filters, via `if (item.term && item.definition)`, and :65 writes the object unchanged. src/Utils/i18n.js init sets no `returnEmptyString: false`; package-lock pins i18next 24.2.2. src/locales/tr.json is 105 lines vs gb.json's 178 (tr lacks the notifications block and the #1889 auth strings). A default manual run (tr,en) exports tr successfully and pushes it.
defects.notes: To count, a comment must say that untranslated terms come back from POEditor as empty strings, are written into the locale file, and show blank text instead of falling back to gb/English. Acceptable fixes it might propose: filter empty values, or use filters=translated or fallback_language. A near-miss that does not count is R3, which argues the opposite: keep empty definitions in the array path. Generic 'validate the export' comments do not count either.

defects.title: One-way download sync overwrites locale files wholesale, deleting keys developers add in the repo before they reach POEditor
defects.statement: The workflow only downloads. It replaces src/locales/<lang>.json with POEditor's export (cp temp/* src/locales/) and pushes the result straight to the branch. The script does no merge with the existing file and no upload. Developers in this repo add strings by editing gb.json and tr.json directly in PRs, so every sync deletes any key not yet entered in POEditor and pushes that deletion. The affected components then show raw keys, and for gb, the fallback language, there is no fallback left.
defects.evidence: poeditor-sync.yml:83 `cp -r temp/* src/locales/`, :90-92 `git add src/locales/*.json` / `git commit` / `git push`. script:65 `fs.writeJson(outputPath, formattedTranslations, ...)` writes only what POEditor returned. History at the merge base shows direct locale edits: d40507e (+30 gb.json), 93462d7 (+34 gb.json), a72d002 (gb.json + tr.json). i18n.js:24 `fallbackLng: primaryLanguage` ("gb").
defects.notes: To count, a comment must say the sync replaces the repo's locale files with the POEditor export, with no merge and no upload of repo-side terms, so keys added directly in the repo are lost or reverted on the next run. Near-misses that do not count: the 'empty {} export' comments (R13-R16), which are about an empty export rather than repo-side keys being overwritten, and formatting or ordering churn.

defects.title: Workflow pushes with GITHUB_TOKEN but requests no contents: write permission
defects.statement: The Commit step runs `git push` with the checkout's GITHUB_TOKEN, but the workflow and job declare no `permissions:` block. On a repo or org whose default workflow token is read-only (GitHub's default for newer orgs and repos), the job downloads and commits and then fails on the push with a 403. Translations are never published.
defects.evidence: poeditor-sync.yml has no `permissions:` key anywhere. Line 28 is `token: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}` and line 92 is `git push`. There are no other workflows in the repo at the merge base, so nothing shows the repo's default token setting.
defects.notes: To count, a comment must say the workflow needs `permissions: contents: write`, or equivalent, for the push, because the default GITHUB_TOKEN may be read-only. Near-misses that do not count: comments about which branch is pushed to (R19-R22), and token-exposure or supply-chain comments (R11).

defects.title: LANGUAGES is split on ',' without trimming or dropping empties, so 'tr, en' or a trailing comma requests ' en' or ''
defects.statement: The workflow_dispatch languages input is free text, and the script only splits it on ','. An operator who types 'tr, en' or leaves a trailing comma sends ' en' or '' as the POEditor language. That either fails the whole run (exit 1 after the first bad export) or writes an oddly named temp/' en'.json, which is copied into src/locales and loaded by the i18n glob as a new language.
defects.evidence: script:12 `const LANGUAGES = (process.env.LANGUAGES || 'tr,en').split(',');` with no `.map(s => s.trim()).filter(Boolean)`. The values are used verbatim at :38 `language: language` and :64 `` `${language}.json` ``. The input at workflow:7-10 is free text described as 'comma separated'.
defects.notes: To count, a comment must say the language list is not trimmed or filtered, so spaces or empty entries produce invalid or oddly named language codes. Near-misses that do not count: the en/gb default mismatch (D1) and generic 'validate env vars' comments (dataset ref 1).

defects.title: json (array) export conversion keys on item.term only, ignoring context, so nested keys collapse and collide
defects.statement: The workflow offers format=json as a supported input. For the array that export returns, the script builds a flat map keyed only by item.term and ignores item.context. POEditor stores the repo's nested keys (notifications.slack.label, notifications.discord.label, ...) as a term plus a parent-path context. Terms like label, description, webhookLabel and webhookPlaceholder therefore overwrite each other, and the nesting that t('notifications.slack.label') needs is lost. That breaks the notification-modal strings for any locale synced with format=json.
defects.evidence: script:56-58 `translations.forEach(item => { if (item.term && item.definition) { formattedTranslations[item.term] = item.definition; } })`, which never reads context. workflow:12 `description: "Export format (key_value_json or json)"`. src/locales/gb.json nests `"notifications": { "slack": { "label" ... }, "discord": { "label" ... } }`, and NotificationIntegrationModal.jsx:33 calls `t('notifications.slack.label')`.
defects.notes: To count, a comment must say the array/json conversion drops context or nesting, so nested keys are flattened or terms collide and the locale no longer matches the nested lookups. A near-miss that does not count is R2, which only asks whether definitions can be objects (plurals). Comments about dropping empty definitions (R3) do not count either.

mudler__LocalAI@e466450.pr_summary: The PR adds two double timing fields in milliseconds, timing_prompt_processing and timing_token_generation, to the gRPC Reply proto. The llama.cpp grpc-server fills them from llama.cpp's final-response `timings` object (prompt_ms / predicted_ms), and they flow through backend.TokenUsage and ComputeChoices into schema.OpenAIUsage as omitempty JSON fields. Chat, completion and edit copy them into the response only when the request carries a `LocalAI-Extra-Usage` header. The PR also adds a `LOCALAI_MACHINE_TAG` run option. When the option is unset, WithMachineTag falls back to os.Hostname(). About 30 individual HTTP handlers send the tag back in a `LocalAI-Machine-Tag` response header, each with its own hand-written c.Set line. ListModelsEndpoint gains an appConfig parameter for this. While refactoring the non-streaming /v1/completions loop, the PR replaced the prompt/completion token accumulation with timing accumulation, so every non-streaming completion now reports zero token usage.

defects.title: Non-streaming /v1/completions now always reports 0 prompt/completion/total tokens
defects.statement: In CompletionEndpoint's non-streaming loop, the PR deleted `totalTokenUsage.Prompt += tokenUsage.Prompt` and `totalTokenUsage.Completion += tokenUsage.Completion` and put the two timing accumulations in their place. totalTokenUsage's token fields therefore stay at their zero value, and the response's usage.prompt_tokens, completion_tokens and total_tokens are always 0. This happens on every non-streaming completion, whether or not the LocalAI-Extra-Usage header is sent, and breaks token accounting for OpenAI-compatible clients.
defects.evidence: Merge base completion.go (non-streaming loop) had `totalTokenUsage.Prompt += tokenUsage.Prompt` / `totalTokenUsage.Completion += tokenUsage.Completion`. At head, lines 183-184 are only `totalTokenUsage.TimingTokenGeneration += tokenUsage.TimingTokenGeneration` / `totalTokenUsage.TimingPromptProcessing += tokenUsage.TimingPromptProcessing`. totalTokenUsage is `backend.TokenUsage{}` (line 163) and nothing else writes Prompt/Completion. Lines 188-192 then build `usage := schema.OpenAIUsage{PromptTokens: totalTokenUsage.Prompt, CompletionTokens: totalTokenUsage.Completion, TotalTokens: totalTokenUsage.Prompt + totalTokenUsage.Completion}`. ComputeChoices (inference.go:53-56) does return populated counts, so they are simply dropped. edit.go:66-70 in the same PR keeps both accumulations and adds the timing lines, which shows the intended pattern. Reached by POST /v1/completions, /completions or /v1/engines/:model/completions with stream=false (routes/openai.go:85-110).
defects.notes: To count, a comment must say that the non-streaming completion path no longer accumulates Prompt/Completion token counts, because the timing lines replaced them, so the reported prompt_tokens/completion_tokens/total_tokens are 0 (or wrong). Pointing at completion.go ~183-184 or the usage block at 188-192 with that mechanism is sufficient. Near-misses that do NOT count: a generic 'add tests for token counts' (R13 mentions the regression only as a reason to add tests and does not identify it on its own); comments about the streaming completion path; comments that only say the timings are summed across prompts.

defects.title: Machine tag defaults to the server hostname and is sent to every client on most endpoints
defects.statement: WithMachineTag falls back to os.Hostname() whenever LOCALAI_MACHINE_TAG is unset, and the CLI always applies it. About 30 handlers then emit it unconditionally as the LocalAI-Machine-Tag response header. As a result, every LocalAI deployment, not only P2P users who opt in, discloses its internal hostname to any API client, including unauthenticated ones under the default no-API-key configuration. The header should be opt-in: sent only when a tag is explicitly configured.
defects.evidence: application_config.go:100-107: `func WithMachineTag(tag string) AppOption { return func(o *ApplicationConfig) { if tag == "" { hostname, _ := os.Hostname(); tag = hostname }; o.MachineTag = tag } }`. run.go:111 always calls `config.WithMachineTag(r.MachineTag)`. Handlers such as chat.go:174 `c.Set("LocalAI-Machine-Tag", startupOptions.MachineTag)`, completion.go:66, list.go:17 and files.go:26/86/125/148/186 set the header with no condition. GET /v1/models (list.go:17) is therefore enough for any client that can reach the port to learn the host's hostname.
defects.notes: To count, a comment must say that the hostname (os.Hostname default) is exposed to clients by default or unconditionally in a response header, as information disclosure, and/or that the machine-tag header should be opt-in or omitted when no tag is configured. Near-misses that do NOT count: 'the os.Hostname error is ignored' (ref 7); 'skip the header when MachineTag is empty', which is about empty values, not disclosure; a nil-appConfig guard; claims that the header should go on outbound backend requests.

defects.title: Machine-tag header set by hand in each handler instead of a middleware; coverage already inconsistent
defects.statement: Instead of one middleware, the LocalAI-Machine-Tag response header is set by a hand-copied `c.Set(...)` line at the top of about 30 individual handlers. Coverage is already inconsistent. The ElevenLabs text-to-speech and sound-generation inference endpoints, /v1/tokenize, /stores/*, the gallery, backend-monitor, /system and /version routes never send it, while ChatEndpoint sets it twice. Clients that use the tag to identify which P2P machine served a request get no tag from those routes. Every future endpoint must also remember the line or silently lose the tag.

It has no match in core/http/endpoints/elevenlabs/* or in the tokenize/stores handlers. Those are registered at routes/elevenlabs.go:16 (`/v1/text-to-speech/:voice-id`) and :18 (`/v1/sound-generation`), and at routes/localai.go:41-44 (`/stores/*`) and :70 (`/v1/tokenize`). core/http/app.go:138-168 registers no shared middleware for the header.

Or: specific routes (ElevenLabs TTS/sound-generation, tokenize, stores, etc.) are missing the machine-tag header, so coverage is inconsistent. Either half counts. Near-misses that do NOT count: a comment only about the redundant second `c.Set` at chat.go:330 (ref 10 / R17), since that is an idempotent nit; CORS ExposeHeaders comments; nil-appConfig comments.

Unlike its neighbours, it also lacks the un-prefixed env alias, a MACHINE_TAG alongside LOCALAI_MACHINE_TAG.

defects.notes: To count, a comment must point out that the new MachineTag flag's help string is a TODO placeholder (user-visible in --help) or that it is otherwise undocumented or unfinished. A comment only about the missing group or env alias, without the placeholder, is a weak match. Near-misses: general 'document the timing units' comments (ref 0 / R1-R3), which are about the proto fields, not this flag.
