alibaba__spring-ai-alibaba@4bc7305.pr_summary: Hotfix to spring-ai-alibaba-jmanus with five changes. (1) The module version goes from 0.1.0 to 0.1.1. (2) Agent save is fixed by giving the deprecated DynamicAgentEntity.systemPrompt a " " default, dropping nullable=false, and having AgentServiceImpl.mergePrompts write " " instead of null. That avoids the NPE and the NOT NULL violation on create, scan and update, but the inverted `!= null || !trim().isEmpty()` guard is left in place. (3) InputTextAction now uses Locator.fill("") + pressSequentially(delay 100). If that fails it falls back to fill(text), then to a raw JS `el.value = ...; dispatchEvent('input')`, and reports success in every case. (4) MoveToAndClickAction now does window.scrollTo(x - vw/2, y - vh/2) before mouse.click(x, y). In debug mode it also injects and removes a red marker dot. (5) NavigateAction adds "https://" to any URL that does not start with lowercase http:// or https://.

defects.title: move_to_and_click scrolls the page, then clicks the unadjusted (x,y), so it hits the wrong element
defects.statement: The action now calls window.scrollTo(x - viewportWidth/2, y - viewportHeight/2) and then still clicks at the original (x, y). Playwright's mouse.click uses viewport coordinates, and callers get (x, y) from get_element_position, which is Locator.boundingBox() and so also viewport-relative. Whenever the scroll moves the page, the click lands on different content. That covers any target right of or below the viewport centre on a scrollable page. It also covers any page that was already scrolled, because scrollTo is absolute and snaps it back. The merge base clicked (x, y) without scrolling, which was correct for this flow.
defects.evidence: MoveToAndClickAction.java:49-52 `int scrollX = Math.max(0, x - page.viewportSize().width / 2); int scrollY = Math.max(0, y - page.viewportSize().height / 2); page.evaluate("(args) => window.scrollTo({left: args[0], top: args[1], behavior: 'instant'})", new Object[] { scrollX, scrollY });` then :69-70 `page.mouse().move(x, y); page.mouse().click(x, y);`, and no scroll offset is subtracted. The coordinates come from GetElementPositionByNameAction.java:124-131 `box = nthLocator.boundingBox(); int x = (int) (box.x + box.width / 2); int y = (int) (box.y + box.height / 2);`. That value is viewport-relative, and the action's own highlight uses `position = 'fixed'`, which confirms it. Example 1: default 1280x720 viewport, page at scroll 0, target at (1000,600). The code scrolls to (360,240), so the target moves to viewport (640,360), and the click at (1000,600) hits something else. Example 2: the agent has scrolled down 1000px and the target is at (500,300). scrollTo(0,0) jumps back to the top of the page, and the click at (500,300) hits top-of-page content. Path: BrowserUseTool.run -> case "move_to_and_click" -> MoveToAndClickAction.execute. If the coordinates were read as document coordinates the click would still be wrong, because the target would then sit at the viewport centre, not at (x,y).
defects.notes: To count, a comment must say that the new scroll moves the page before the click, but the click still uses the same (x,y), which are viewport coordinates from boundingBox/get_element_position. The click therefore lands on the wrong element (or the coordinates are not adjusted by the scroll offset). It is enough to note the mismatch between the scroll and the unadjusted click coordinates. Near-misses that do not count: a viewportSize() null-check comment (ref 5); comments only about the debug marker's position:absolute placement; generic 'scrolling may be unnecessary' remarks that never say the click target shifts.

defects.title: input_text falls back to a raw JS el.value assignment and reports success for fields that rejected input
defects.statement: When both Playwright fill attempts fail, the action runs `el.value = value; el.dispatchEvent(new Event('input'))` and returns "成功输入" (success). Fill fails on disabled, readonly and hidden fields and on non-text types such as checkbox or radio. The JS fallback skips the editability and type checks, so it forces a value into a field the user could not edit, and the agent is told the input succeeded. The typing and change events some form handlers or controlled inputs need are also skipped. Both earlier exceptions are dropped without logging. At the merge base these cases threw and were reported as "Browser action 'input_text' failed". Now they wait through up to two 30s actionability timeouts and then report a false success.
defects.evidence: InputTextAction.java:62-75 `try { elementLocator.fill(""); ... elementLocator.pressSequentially(text, options); } catch (Exception e) { try { elementLocator.fill(""); elementLocator.fill(text); } catch (Exception e2) { ... elementLocator.evaluate("(el, value) => { el.value = value; el.dispatchEvent(new Event('input', { bubbles: true })); }", text);` and :88 `return new ToolExecuteResult("成功输入: '" + text + ...)`. The only type check is the tag name at :55 (`!"input".equals(tagName) && !"textarea".equals(tagName)`). The registry indexes every `a, button, input, select, textarea` with no visibility or enabled filter (InteractiveElementRegistry.java:42, :100-112), so disabled, readonly, hidden and checkbox inputs can be selected. At the merge base, `handle.click(); handle.fill("");` threw for these, and BrowserUseTool.run:272-274 returned a failure result.
defects.notes: To count, a comment must say that the JS `el.value` fallback bypasses Playwright's editability/actionability (or type) checks and still returns success. The result is a false success for disabled, readonly or hidden inputs, or input that is not accepted, or form handlers that never see the change. Near-misses that do not count: 'the second fill("") is redundant' (ref 3, R9); unused-import comments; 'add tests' (R8); a remark that only says the exceptions should be logged, without the false-success consequence.

defects.title: navigate prepends https:// to every URL without a lowercase http(s) prefix, breaking other schemes
defects.statement: The new auto-prefix rewrites any URL that does not start with lowercase "http://" or "https://". about:blank becomes https://about:blank, file:///tmp/x.html becomes https://file:///tmp/x.html, and data:, ftp:// and chrome:// URLs are broken the same way. An uppercase HTTP://example.com becomes https://HTTP://example.com. At the merge base page.navigate received these unchanged and handled them. Now they fail to navigate or go somewhere unintended.
defects.evidence: NavigateAction.java:42-44 `if (!url.startsWith("http://") && !url.startsWith("https://")) { url = "https://" + url; }` then :46 `page.navigate(url, ...)`. BrowserUseTool.java:223-224 forwards the URL the agent supplies directly to NavigateAction. The merge base passed the URL to page.navigate unchanged.
defects.notes: To count, a comment must say the prefix check only recognises (lowercase) http/https, so URLs that already have another scheme get mangled. Examples are about:, file:, data:, ftp:, or uppercase HTTP. The fix is to prefix only when no scheme is present. A comment that only mentions protocol-relative '//host' also counts, since it is the same mechanism. Near-misses that do not count: 'URL validation should be stricter' with no mangling example, and 'url could be null' (already checked at :38).

defects.title: Agent-save fix uses a " " sentinel instead of fixing the inverted `||` guard, so the deprecated-prompt branch fires on every read and write
defects.statement: The NPE the PR works around comes from mergePrompts' guard `getSystemPrompt() != null || !getSystemPrompt().trim().isEmpty()`. That guard is true for every non-null value and dereferences null. Rather than fix it, the PR makes the field never null (a " " default, and " " written back as the 'cleared' value). The cleared state therefore still satisfies the guard. Every mapToAgentConfig and updateEntityFromConfig, for every agent including brand-new ones with no legacy prompt, re-enters the deprecation branch. Each time it logs a WARN claiming the SystemPrompt is non-empty and was merged, and prints the whole next-step prompt.
defects.evidence: AgentServiceImpl.java:190 `if (entity.getSystemPrompt() != null || !entity.getSystemPrompt().trim().isEmpty()) {` ... :197-199 `log.warn("Agent[{}]的SystemPrompt不为空， 但属性已经废弃...本次将agent 的内容合并... 当前制定的值: {}", agentName, nextPrompt);` :200 `entity.setSystemPrompt(" ");`. DynamicAgentEntity.java:45-47 `@Column(length = 40000) @Deprecated private String systemPrompt = " ";`. mergePrompts is called from createAgent:94, updateEntityFromConfig:168 and mapToAgentConfig:153. Creating one agent therefore warns three times, and each admin getAllAgents/getAgentById call (AgentController:46/51) warns once per agent, forever, even though " " is not a prompt.
defects.notes: To count, a comment must identify the mergePrompts guard at :190 (`!= null || !...trim().isEmpty()`) as the real defect the " " sentinel papers over, so it should be a null-safe && / isBlank check. It may name either consequence: the misleading deprecation warning firing for every agent on every read or save, or the guard still NPE-ing on null now that the column is nullable. Near-misses that do not count: 'use "" instead of " "' alone (ref 0/ref 1, which changes nothing because "" is also non-null); 'add a comment explaining the space'; and claims that " " bypasses some validation. Credit rests on identifying the inverted || guard and its misleading WARN; a claimed NPE path does not count (nothing can make systemPrompt null after this PR).

defects.title: Debug marker cleanup is not guaranteed, and its failure can turn a successful click into a reported failure
defects.statement: In debug mode (manus.browser.debug=true) the red marker is removed by a page.evaluate placed in the same try block right after mouse.click, not in a finally block. If the click's navigation has already destroyed the page's execution context, that evaluate throws. The catch then returns "Failed to click at position" for a click that happened and skips new-tab detection. If move or click throws, the removal is skipped and the dot stays in the DOM. Because of the `if (!dot)` guard, the next debug click reuses that stale dot rather than repositioning it.
defects.evidence: MoveToAndClickAction.java:57-65 inject: `let dot = document.getElementById(id); if (!dot) { dot = document.createElement('div'); ... document.body.appendChild(dot); }`. Then :69-70 `page.mouse().move(x, y); page.mouse().click(x, y);`, then :73-77 `if (isDebug) { page.evaluate("(id) => { const dot = document.getElementById(id); if (dot) dot.remove(); }", ...); }`. All of this is inside `try { ... } catch (Exception e) { ... return new ToolExecuteResult("Failed to click at position (" + x + ", " + y + ")"); }` (:79-82), which returns before the new-window check at :85-103. There is no finally block. Only reached when manus.browser.debug is true (default "false", ManusProperties.java:93-96).
defects.notes: To count, a comment must say either that the marker removal is not in a finally or guarded cleanup, so the dot leaks when the click path throws, or that the post-click removal evaluate can itself throw (for example after navigation) and make a successful click report failure. Near-misses that do not count: 'extract the marker JS into helper methods' (ref 7), and the Boolean-unboxing NPE on getBrowserDebug (ref 4).

excluded.reason: Naming/comment taste. The " " default behaves the same as "" in the only check that reads it (AgentServiceImpl:190). The real guard defect is D4, and this note does not raise it.

Wrong claim. No validation tells " " apart from "": the only check (:190) is true for any non-null value and trims anyway. Switching to "" changes nothing. The actual guard bug (D4) is not what this note says.
Unused import (WaitForSelectorState; Random and ElementHandle are also unused now). A lint-level nit: the pom has no checkstyle, and spring-javaformat validate does not fail on unused imports.
Nit. The second fill("") is redundant because fill(text) replaces the value, but removing it changes no behaviour. If fill("") fails, fill(text) would fail the same actionability check.

Unreachable. ConfigService.initializeConfig seeds manus.browser.debug with defaultValue "false", so getBrowserDebug() returns Boolean.valueOf("false"), not null. The same unboxing already exists in GetElementPositionByNameAction:87.

Unreachable. Pages come from browser.newPage() (ChromeDriverService:128) and popups in the same context, which use the default 1280x720 viewport, so viewportSize() is non-null. The code never creates a context with a null viewport.
Readability refactor suggestion (extract the debug-marker JS into methods); not a defect.
Request to add tests; not a defect.
Same as ref 3: the redundant second fill("") is a nit. fill(text) would hit the same actionability wait, so there is no behavioural consequence.

excluded.source: hunt:pressSequentially at a fixed 100ms per character exceeds the default 30s action timeout for texts over about 300 characters
excluded.reason: Not a regression. The merge-base code typed per character with about 50-149ms delay plus 20-69ms sleep, roughly 145ms per character, so long texts were already slower. At head a timeout falls through to fill(text), which leaves the correct final value. Per-keystroke handler side effects also happened with the old per-character type().

openai__codex@8c952af.pr_summary: "Never store requests" (openai/codex #3212) removes the `disable_response_storage` option everywhere it appeared: Config, ConfigToml, ConfigProfile, ConfigOverrides, TurnContext, ConfigureSession, the MCP `Profile` type and the exec/tui/mcp-server callers. It also removes `Prompt.store`. Every Responses API request now sends `store: false` and, when reasoning is on, asks for `reasoning.encrypted_content`. The PR adds `#[serde(skip_serializing)]` to the `id` field of every `ResponseItem` variant (Message, Reasoning, LocalShellCall, FunctionCall, CustomToolCall, WebSearchCall), so item ids are never sent back to the API. Test expectations drop `"id": null`, and the PR deletes the store assertions.

defects.title: codex-core unit tests no longer compile: `store` is removed from the ResponsesApiRequest test literals but the field still exists
defects.statement: The PR keeps `pub(crate) store: bool` on `ResponsesApiRequest` (client_common.rs:128) but deletes `store: true,` from both struct literals in the client_common.rs test module. Neither literal uses `..Default::default()`, and the struct derives only Debug and Serialize. The lib's test target therefore fails with E0063 (missing field `store`), which breaks `cargo test` and `cargo clippy --tests` for codex-core in CI.
defects.evidence: Head client_common.rs:117-136 `#[derive(Debug, Serialize)] pub(crate) struct ResponsesApiRequest<'a> { ... pub(crate) reasoning: Option<Reasoning>, pub(crate) store: bool, pub(crate) stream: bool, ... }`. The diff removes `-            store: true,` from both test literals. At head, `let req = ResponsesApiRequest { model: "gpt-5", instructions: "i", input: &input, tools: &tools, tool_choice: "auto", parallel_tool_calls: false, reasoning: None, stream: true, include: vec![], prompt_cache_key: None, text: ... };` (lines 190 and 219) has no `store` and no `..` base. The production site client.rs:198 still sets `store: false`, so the field is live. CI (.github/workflows/rust-ci.yml:148) runs `cargo clippy ... --tests -- -D warnings`, and :168 runs `cargo test --all-features`.
defects.notes: To count, a finding must say that the ResponsesApiRequest literals in the client_common.rs tests no longer initialize the still-required `store` field, so the core test target fails to compile (missing field). Either literal, or both, is enough. Near-misses that do not count: comments about the misleading `store` doc comment being removed, or suggestions to drop the `store` field as dead or constant without saying the tests fail to compile.

defects.title: mcp-server integration tests no longer compile: they still set the removed `Profile.disable_response_storage` field
defects.statement: The PR removes `disable_response_storage` from `codex_protocol::mcp_protocol::Profile`, but the unchanged `codex-rs/mcp-server/tests/suite/config.rs` still builds a `Profile { ..., disable_response_storage: Some(false), ... }`. That file is compiled into the mcp-server `all` integration-test binary through `tests/all.rs` -> `mod suite;` -> `mod config;`, so the mcp-server test build fails with E0560 (no field `disable_response_storage`) and CI fails.
defects.evidence: Head mcp_protocol.rs:368 `pub struct Profile { pub model, pub model_provider, pub approval_policy, pub model_reasoning_effort, pub model_reasoning_summary, pub model_verbosity, pub chatgpt_base_url }`, from which the diff removes `-    pub disable_response_storage: Option<bool>,`. At head, mcp-server/tests/suite/config.rs:114 has `disable_response_storage: Some(false),` inside `Profile { model: Some("gpt-4o".into()), ... }`. `git grep disable_response_storage <head>` still finds this file, and the PR does not touch it. tests/all.rs has `mod suite;` and tests/suite/mod.rs has `mod config;`.
defects.notes: To count, a finding must say that the mcp-server test `Profile` literal (tests/suite/config.rs) still sets `disable_response_storage`, which no longer exists on `Profile`, so that test target fails to compile. Near-misses that do not count: saying only that the TOML fixture line `disable_response_storage = false` (config.rs:54) is stale. It is silently ignored because Profile/ConfigProfile have no deny_unknown_fields. Generic 'update the tests' remarks that do not name the compile failure also do not count.

defects.title: Reasoning items are written to rollouts without their required `id`, so resumed sessions silently drop all reasoning
defects.statement: `ResponseItem::Reasoning { #[serde(skip_serializing)] id: String, ... }` has no `#[serde(default)]`, unlike the other skipped ids, which are `Option`s and default to None. The rollout writer serializes ResponseItems with the same serde impl, so every persisted Reasoning line lacks `id`. On resume, `serde_json::from_value::<ResponseItem>` fails with 'missing field `id`', and `get_rollout_history` only logs a warning and skips the line. Every reasoning item, including its `encrypted_content`, is therefore lost when a session is resumed from the TUI (resume/continue), through MCP resumeConversation or through experimental_resume. With store now always false, that encrypted content is the only way the model's prior reasoning carries across turns.
defects.evidence: models.rs:50-56 at head: `Reasoning { #[serde(skip_serializing)] id: String, summary: Vec<...>, #[serde(default, ...)] content: ..., encrypted_content: Option<String> }`. Writer: recorder.rs:293-297 `RolloutCmd::AddItems(items) => for item in items { if is_persisted_response_item(&item) { writer.write_line(&item).await?; } }`, and write_line (:329) uses `serde_json::to_string(item)`. rollout/policy.rs:8 lists `ResponseItem::Reasoning { .. }` as persisted. Reader: recorder.rs:189-197 `match serde_json::from_value::<ResponseItem>(v.clone()) { Ok(item) => ..., Err(e) => { warn!("failed to parse item: {v:?}, error: {e}"); } }`. Reasoning items are recorded in codex.rs:1520-1533 and reach the rollout via record_conversation_items. Resume callers: conversation_manager.rs:134 (used by tui/src/app.rs:90 and mcp-server codex_message_processor.rs:613) and :70 (experimental_resume).
defects.notes: To count, a finding must connect the non-optional `Reasoning.id: String` + `skip_serializing` to local persistence: rollout items are written without `id` and cannot be deserialized back (missing required field), so resume drops reasoning items. Accepted fixes include `#[serde(default)]`/Option, or a separate wire representation. Near-misses that do not count: claiming API responses fail to parse because they contain `id` (skip_serializing does not affect deserialization, so that is wrong); vague 'id may be dropped in other serialization paths' remarks that never say the item becomes unreadable or lost on resume; and complaints only that the field should be Option for consistency.

defects.title: Now-unused `request_body` bindings in two auth tests fail `cargo clippy --tests -D warnings`
defects.statement: In `prefers_chatgpt_token_when_config_prefers_chatgpt` and `prefers_apikey_when_config_prefers_apikey_even_with_chatgpt_tokens`, the PR replaces the only use of `request_body` (the store assertion) with a comment but keeps `let request_body = request.body_json::<serde_json::Value>().unwrap();`. That triggers rustc's `unused_variables` warning, which CI's clippy step promotes to an error with `-- -D warnings`. The core test job therefore still fails after the compile errors are fixed. The replacement comment also says 'store flag removed' even though every request still sends `store: false`.
defects.evidence: Head core/tests/suite/client.rs:579-581 `let request = &server.received_requests().await.unwrap()[0]; let request_body = request.body_json::<serde_json::Value>().unwrap(); // store flag removed; responses are never stored.`, followed by `}`. Lines 660-662 are the same. The diff removes `assert!(!request_body["store"].as_bool().unwrap(), ...)` and `assert!(request_body["store"].as_bool().unwrap(), ...)`. core/Cargo.toml has `[lints] workspace = true`, with no allow in tests/all.rs or suite/mod.rs. rust-ci.yml:148 runs `cargo clippy --target ... --all-features --tests --profile ... -- -D warnings`.
defects.notes: To count, a finding must say that `request_body` is left unused at client.rs ~580 and/or ~661, which produces an unused-variable warning or clippy -D warnings failure (a dead binding). Near-misses that do not count: comments that only ask to restore or assert `store == false` for coverage without noting that the binding is now unused (a test request); and remarks that the comment wording is misleading.

excluded.reason: Style nit: it objects to the tombstone comment `// Removed: server-side response storage control...` at config.rs:81. The comment is harmless and has no behavioural or maintenance cost.
Wrong premise: the field was deleted, so no field's docs were demoted. Turning the line into `///` as suggested would attach it to `user_instructions` and corrupt that field's docs.
Duplicate of ref 0 (the same tombstone-comment nit for the ConfigToml copy at config.rs:416). Style only.
Duplicate of ref 1 and wrong for the same reason: a `///` at config.rs:416 would become part of the `notify` field's rustdoc.

Wrong mechanism: `skip_serializing` does not affect deserialization, so API payloads that contain `id` still parse at client.rs:509. The suggested `skip_deserializing` fix is also unneeded for that path. The real problem, a missing `id` on rollout resume, is D3, and this ref does not describe it.
Describes a field that does not exist: `FunctionCallOutput` has no `id` at head or at merge base (`FunctionCallOutput { call_id, output }`, models.rs:84-87).

Docs-update requests (docs/config.md and docs/zdr.md still mention `disable_response_storage`). No behavioural consequence: ConfigToml/ConfigProfile have no deny_unknown_fields, so the stale key is silently ignored, and responses are now never stored, which is the ZDR-safe behaviour. Docs requests are out of scope for this benchmark.

Test-coverage requests (restore a `store == false` assertion so a regression would be caught). Neither comment says that `request_body` is now an unused binding that fails clippy -D warnings (D4), so they do not identify a concrete defect.

mpv-player__mpv@0729afe.pr_summary: The PR changes mp_option_change_callback so it no longer runs per-option side effects inline. Each change is appended as a {co, flags} entry to mpctx->option_callbacks. When a queued entry has the same nonzero flags or the same option, the older entry is dropped and the new one goes to the end. The new function mp_option_run_callbacks drains the queue in run_playloop and mp_idle, right after mp_process_input. A second commit moves startup IPC initialization out of the callback and into mp_initialize (main.c:415). As a result, the startup call mp_option_change_callback(mpctx, NULL, UPDATE_OPTS_MASK, false), which used to run every handler once inside mp_initialize, now only queues an entry. That entry runs at the first mp_idle or playloop iteration, and nothing wakes the core when an entry is queued.

defects.title: The startup 'run all update handlers' pass is only queued, so it runs against live playback state after playback has started
defects.statement: mp_initialize's 'Run all update handlers' call now only queues {co=NULL, flags=UPDATE_OPTS_MASK}. The handlers therefore run at the first mp_idle, which for a CLI run with no clients (no user scripts, Linux) is inside play_current_file's open loop, after stop_play was reset to 0. There the UPDATE_DVB_PROG branch sets stop_play=PT_CURRENT_ENTRY. That aborts the first file's open, and mp_play_files replays the entry, so the file opens twice, clients get spurious start-file/end-file events, and pipes/stdin lose the data the first open consumed. In the same pass, UPDATE_VO destroys and recreates any VO that force-window already made (idle+force-window, pseudo-gui with no file, force-window=immediate). Before the PR both branches were no-ops, because they ran in mp_initialize while stop_play was PT_NEXT_ENTRY and before any VO existed. The same deferral also means the initial pass no longer completes before the first file: builtin scripts (osc, ytdl_hook, auto_profiles) are created only by UPDATE_BUILTIN_SCRIPTS and are neither loaded nor waited on before the first file's hooks (the mp_play_files script-wait gate is skipped when there are no user scripts), and config-file logging/terminal settings from UPDATE_TERM apply late, losing early log messages.
defects.evidence: main.c:387 `mp_option_change_callback(mpctx, NULL, UPDATE_OPTS_MASK, false);` now just reaches `MP_TARRAY_APPEND(mpctx, mpctx->option_callbacks, ...)` (command.c:7723). UPDATE_OPTS_MASK includes UPDATE_DVB_PROG (m_option.h:440,452). mp_create sets `.stop_play = PT_NEXT_ENTRY` (main.c:280), so the old synchronous run was a no-op. With zero clients, mp_clients_all_initialized returns true (client.c:209-221), so mp_play_files skips its mp_idle wait (loadfile.c:2071-2076). idle_loop does nothing when not idle. play_current_file does `mpctx->stop_play = 0;` (1621), and process_hooks does not idle when no hooks exist (mp_hook_test_completion returns true, command.c:191-207). The first mp_idle is in `while (!atomic_load(&mpctx->open_done)) { mp_idle(mpctx); if (mpctx->stop_play) mp_abort_playback_async(mpctx); }` (1243-1247). mp_idle calls mp_option_run_callbacks (playloop.c:1305), which runs `if (flags & UPDATE_DVB_PROG) { if (!mpctx->stop_play) mpctx->stop_play = PT_CURRENT_ENTRY; }` (command.c:7827-7830). Playback then terminates, and mp_play_files does `else if (mpctx->stop_play == PT_CURRENT_ENTRY) new_entry = mpctx->playlist->current;`. Likewise `if (flags & UPDATE_VO && mpctx->video_out) { uninit_video_out(mpctx); handle_force_window(mpctx, true); ...}` (7783-7791) fires after idle_loop's `handle_force_window(mpctx, true)` (playloop.c:1322) or main.c:427's force_vo==2 path already created the VO.
defects.notes: To count, a comment must say that the startup UPDATE_OPTS_MASK 'run all update handlers' call (main.c:383-387) is now only queued and runs later, together with ANY one consequence: UPDATE_DVB_PROG aborting and reloading the first file, UPDATE_VO recreating the force-window VO, builtin scripts/hooks missing or not waited on for the first file, or config-file logging applied late. A generic 'initialization is deferred' that names the startup handler pass counts; a comment that names none of this does not.

defects.title: Queued option changes never wake the core: synchronous property/option sets (mpv_set_property, IPC set_property, script mp.set_property) do not take effect while the player sleeps
defects.statement: mp_option_change_callback now only appends to the queue and never calls mp_wakeup_core or interrupts the dispatch queue. Synchronous client paths (mpv_set_property, mpv_set_option, and through them JSON IPC set_property and Lua/JS mp.set_property*) run under mp_dispatch_lock/unlock. Unlocking does not end the core's timed wait in mp_dispatch_queue_process. The queued handlers (set_pause_state, update_track_switch, audio_update_volume, VO/OSD refresh, ...) therefore do not run until something unrelated wakes the core. While paused or idle that can be indefinitely: for example, JSON-IPC set_property sid while paused does not switch subtitles, and a libmpv client that doesn't observe 'pause' calling set_property pause=no stays paused. Before the PR these handlers ran synchronously, and several of them woke the core themselves.
defects.evidence: The new callback body ends with `MP_TARRAY_APPEND(mpctx, mpctx->option_callbacks, mpctx->num_option_callbacks, callback);` and contains no wakeup. The path is mpv_set_property -> `run_locked(ctx, setproperty_fn, &req)` -> `mp_dispatch_lock(...); fn(fn_data); mp_dispatch_unlock(...)`. mp_dispatch_unlock only decrements lock_requests and broadcasts, and the process loop then re-enters `} else if (queue->wait > 0 && !queue->interrupted) { mp_cond_timedwait_until(...) }`. Only mp_dispatch_append/mp_dispatch_interrupt set `interrupted`. The only incidental wake is mp_client_property_change's `if (any_pending) mp_dispatch_adjust_timeout(mpctx->dispatch, 0);`, which fires only if some client observes that exact property. Callbacks run only after mp_wait_events returns (playloop.c:1286-1292, 1303-1305). Before the PR, set_pause_state called `mp_wakeup_core(mpctx)` (playloop.c:175) and update_track_switch called `mp_wakeup_core(mpctx)` (command.c:7688) synchronously from the callback. IPC uses mpv_set_property (input/ipc.c:243), and Lua uses it too (lua.c:635-665).
defects.notes: To count, a comment must say that queuing the option callback does not wake the core (no mp_wakeup_core or dispatch interrupt). As a result, a change made through a synchronous client/IPC/script set while the player is paused or idle isn't applied until an unrelated event wakes the loop, possibly never. Near-misses that do NOT count: generic claims that deferral adds 'latency until the next playloop iteration' or 'hundreds of ms' without the no-wakeup / stuck-while-idle mechanism (dataset ref 6); requests to confirm reentrancy (ref 7).

defects.title: Setting aid/vid/sid no longer switches the track synchronously: a read right after the set, and the command's OSD message, report the previous track
defects.statement: For aid/vid/sid/secondary-sid, SET goes through mp_property_generic_option, which only writes the option and queues the callback; update_track_switch now runs later in mp_option_run_callbacks. GET and PRINT for these properties read mpctx->current_track while playback is initialized. So `set sid 2` / `cycle-values sid ...` (input.conf, IPC text commands) shows the old track in its OSD message, and a get_property right after a successful set_property returns the old track id until the queue drains, which is indefinitely while paused (see D3). Before the PR, update_track_switch ran inside the SET call.
defects.evidence: mp_property_switch_track: `struct track *track = mpctx->current_track[order][type]; ... case M_PROPERTY_GET: if (mpctx->playback_initialized) { *(int *)arg = track ? track->user_tid : -2; }`, and PRINT formats the same `track`. M_PROPERTY_SET falls through to `return mp_property_generic_option(...)`, which calls m_config_set_option_raw -> callback -> queue. `if (opt_ptr == &opts->stream_id[order][type]) update_track_switch(mpctx, order, type);` (7930-7931) now runs only in mp_option_run_callbacks. change_property_cmd calls `mp_property_do(...)` and then immediately show_property_status -> show_property_osd, which expands `"%s: ${%s}"` at call time via mp_property_expand_string (4812-4814).
defects.notes: To count, a comment must say that because update_track_switch is deferred, setting aid/vid/sid (or another option whose effect is read back through derived state) followed immediately by a read or by the command's OSD message reports the old track, which breaks read-after-write for property sets. Near-misses that do NOT count: generic 'side effects are delayed' remarks with no stale read-back or OSD consequence; the missing wakeup itself (that is D3).

defects.title: Coalescing a round-trip hidpi-window-scale toggle leaves one unpaired relative resize, so the window is rescaled although the option ends where it started
defects.statement: update_hidpi_window_scale does not re-derive the window size from state. It applies a relative resize: it multiplies the current unfullscreened window size by the cached HiDPI scale when the option is true, and by the inverse when it is false. The new queue keeps only the newest entry for an option, and the handler reads the option's value at drain time. So if hidpi-window-scale is changed and changed back before the queue drains (true→false→true, or any even number of toggles), only one callback survives. It applies a single ×scale (or ×1/scale) to a window whose size is still correct, so the window is resized by the display scale factor (for example doubled or halved on a 2x display) even though the option's net change is zero. Before the PR each change ran synchronously and the two resizes cancelled out: the x11, wayland and win32 VOs update their stored size synchronously on VOCTRL_SET_UNFS_WINDOW_SIZE, so the second GET saw the first resize. Both changes reach the queue before one drain whenever they land in the same batch. That happens with a single command that sets the option twice (load-config-file of a file or profile that sets it twice), with `;`-chained set/cycle commands (mp_process_input runs every queued command before mp_option_run_callbacks), and with a script or IPC client that sets the option and restores it while the core sleeps (the queue is not drained until an unrelated wakeup, see D3).
defects.evidence: The coalescing loop in mp_option_change_callback (command.c:7706-7724), `if (mpctx->option_callbacks[i].co && opt_ptr == mpctx->option_callbacks[i].co->data) drop = true;`, overwrites the older same-option entry and keeps a single one. The drain calls `if (opt_ptr == &opts->vo->hidpi_window_scale) update_hidpi_window_scale(mpctx, opts->vo->hidpi_window_scale);` (7898-7899) with the value current at drain time. update_hidpi_window_scale computes `double scale = hidpi_scale ? cmd->cached_window_scale : 1 / cmd->cached_window_scale;`, then reads VOCTRL_GET_UNFS_WINDOW_SIZE, does `s[0] *= scale; s[1] *= scale;` and calls VOCTRL_SET_UNFS_WINDOW_SIZE (2781-2799), which is relative to the current size. m_config only notifies on a real change (m_config_core.c:802 `!m_option_equal(...)`), so a round trip produces exactly two queued changes, and coalescing collapses them into one. Base (e4b64fb) command.c:7870-7871 ran the handler once per change, synchronously, so the two resizes cancelled. mp_process_input loops `for (;;) { cmd = mp_input_read_cmd(...); if (!cmd) break; run_command(...); }` before `mp_option_run_callbacks(mpctx);` (playloop.c:1290-1292, 1304-1305).
defects.notes: To count, a comment must name hidpi-window-scale / update_hidpi_window_scale (or the relative window resize it performs) as a handler that coalescing breaks, because it applies a delta instead of re-deriving state from the final value. It must also name the consequence: changing the option and changing it back before the queue drains leaves one unpaired resize, so the window is rescaled by the HiDPI factor although the option ends where it started. The comment does not need to say that the two resizes cancelled before the PR. Near-misses that do NOT count: a generic 'coalescing may drop intermediate updates' or 'handlers must be idempotent' that names no concrete delta handler; a comment that names a state-based handler (e.g. window-scale / update_window_scale) as the broken one; the flag-collision or interleaving claims excluded as R2/R3; stale read-back after a set (D4) or the missing wakeup (D3).

excluded.reason: Wrong. At iteration i the loop reads option_callbacks[i] before writing slot i, so every original entry is examined. `drop` is sticky, and the loop correctly removes the first match and re-appends the new entry last (command.c:7707-7719). The suggested rewrite is itself broken: it drops every entry after the match and never appends the new callback.
Style/readability preference (extract the loop body into a function). No defect.
Wrong. Head guards both uses: `void *opt_ptr = co ? co->data : NULL;` (command.c:7732), and the coalescing loop checks `option_callbacks[i].co && ...` (7711). No NULL dereference.
Compensated. The second commit initializes IPC in mp_initialize, `mpctx->ipc_ctx = mp_init_ipc(...)` (main.c:415), so dropping `init ||` from the callback is not a regression.

Not a leak. The array is talloc-parented on mpctx, MP_TARRAY_APPEND reuses capacity, and resetting num_option_callbacks=0 reuses the buffer, which is bounded by the peak queue size and freed with mpctx.
NULL is the normal return of mp_init_ipc when no IPC path is configured, and mp_uninit_ipc handles NULL. The old callback stored it unchecked the same way.

Speculative, with the wrong mechanism. Changes made from input commands and async dispatch items are drained in the same iteration (playloop.c:1286-1292), so there is no generic 'hundreds of ms' delay. The real issue is the missing wakeup for synchronous sets (D3), which this comment does not identify.

A 'please confirm reentrancy/boundedness' request with no concrete path. input-commands only queues commands (command.c:7645-7650), handlers use self-notifications, and the per-iteration call is a no-op when the queue is empty.
Readability/style request to make the single-match removal explicit. The behaviour is already correct.

Not reachable. No option has both nonzero UPDATE_* flags and an opt_ptr-specific handler: every opt_ptr-handled option (pause, speed, aid/sid/vid, vf/af, ab-loop, input-commands, ipc, vo window options, ...) has flags 0, and no group change_flags apply to them. Flag-driven handlers read the current global state, so dropping the older entry with equal flags loses nothing. The startup entry (co=NULL, flags=UPDATE_OPTS_MASK) cannot collide by flags with any real option.

Not reachable. A given option always produces the same change mask, so a queue entry can match at most one existing entry, and zero flags never match by flags. Interleaved A,B,A,B yields [A,B], not A,A,B, so run_command_opts cannot run twice this way.
Request to add tests. Not a defect.

ppy__osu@748ab3d.pr_summary: This PR targets pp-dev and is described as a speed-up of the osu! RhythmEvaluator. The old code computed the rhythm-ratio term as `Math.Min(0.5, sin²(π / (min/max)))`. The new code computes `Math.Min(0.5, SmoothstepBellCurve(frac(max/min)))` and adds the helper `DifficultyCalculationUtils.SmoothstepBellCurve(x, mean=0.5, width=0.5)`, which is smoothstep(1-2|x-0.5|). Rewriting the ratio as a fractional part is correct, because sin²(πR) has period 1. The `(long)` cast is safe, since StrainTime is floored at 25 ms, and the helper behaves as its doc says. The one real problem is that smoothstep only approximates sin². The two curves match only at frac = 0 and inside the 0.5 clamp band [0.25, 0.75]. Everywhere else the new value is strictly higher, by up to +0.010 at frac ≈ 0.139. So a PR presented as a pure optimisation also quietly raises the rhythm and speed difficulty, and therefore SR/pp, for off-integer delta ratios.

defects.title: The smoothstep bell curve is not equivalent to sin²: the 'optimisation' changes the rhythm bonus and therefore SR/pp
defects.statement: Before the 0.5 clamp, SmoothstepBellCurve(f) equals 12f²-16f³ for f<0.25 (mirrored for f>0.75). The old term was sin²(πf). The two agree only at f=0 and wherever both are clamped to 0.5 (f in [0.25, 0.75]). For f in (0, 0.25) ∪ (0.75, 1) the new value is always higher, by up to +0.010, so currRatio = 1 + 12·term rises by up to +0.12 (about +4%). Every pair of deltas whose ratio is not a whole or half multiple (e.g. 1.1, 1.125, 1.2, 1.89, 3.2) now gets a larger rhythm multiplier in Speed. The PR is presented as a pure speed optimisation ("9x faster", with a Desmos plot of the curves) with no star-rating or pp diff, although the new curve raises values for off-integer ratios.
defects.evidence: Merge base: `double currRatio = 1.0 + rhythm_ratio_multiplier * Math.Min(0.5, Math.Pow(Math.Sin(Math.PI / deltaDifferenceRatio), 2));`. Head, RhythmEvaluator.cs:71-76: `reverseDeltaDifferenceRatio = Math.Max(prevDelta, currDelta) / Math.Min(prevDelta, currDelta); deltaDifferenceFraction = reverseDeltaDifferenceRatio - (long)reverseDeltaDifferenceRatio; currRatio = 1.0 + rhythm_ratio_multiplier * Math.Min(0.5, DifficultyCalculationUtils.SmoothstepBellCurve(deltaDifferenceFraction));`. Helper, DifficultyCalculationUtils.cs:78-80: `x -= mean; x = x > 0 ? (width - x) : (width + x); return Smoothstep(x, 0, width);`. Smoothstep is 3t²-2t³ (line 93). Evaluated numerically (old → new clamped term): ratio 1.1: 0.0955→0.1040; 1.125: 0.1464→0.1563; 1.2 and 3.2: 0.3455→0.3520; 1.889: 0.1170→0.1262. The maximum difference is +0.0100 at f≈0.139, and the new value is never lower. Path: Speed.StrainValueAt (Speed.cs:45) calls RhythmEvaluator.EvaluateDifficultyOf for every object, and `totalStrain = currentStrain * currentRhythm` feeds the speed rating and SR. Severity is low: the shift is small, common snapped ratios (2, 1.5, 4/3, 5/4) fall at f=0 or inside the clamp band and are unchanged, and pp-dev accepts balance changes. I estimate the objects the change touches in diffcalc-test.osu (78500, 98250, 99875) sit in low-weight strain sections, so the hard-coded SR tests (Within 1e-5) probably still pass. I did not run them.
defects.notes: To count, a comment must say that the new smoothstep bell curve is not a drop-in equivalent of the old sin²(π·ratio) term. It must say that it gives different (higher) values for some fractional delta ratios, so rhythm/speed difficulty, star rating or pp change, meaning the PR is not a pure performance change. Naming a concrete ratio (e.g. 1.125) or the region outside the 0.5 clamp is enough. These do not count: requests for tests (R1, R3); asking for a Version bump or star-rating cache invalidation without saying the curve changes values; saying 'tests may fail' without identifying the curve mismatch; claiming the max/min fractional-part rewrite is mathematically wrong (it is exact, since sin²(πR) has period 1); division-by-zero, long-overflow or precision concerns about the fraction; doc typos; the width==0 edge case; naming or Math.Abs simplification suggestions.

excluded.reason: Unreachable. StrainTime = Math.Max(DeltaTime, MIN_DELTA_TIME=25) (OsuDifficultyHitObject.cs:25,123), so neither division can see 0 or near-0. Smoothstep clamps its normalised input to [0,1] (DifficultyCalculationUtils.cs:91), so overshoot cannot escape, and the (long)-based fraction is exact at these magnitudes. Even a hypothetical infinite ratio gives 0 under the new code, where the old code gave NaN.
Misreads the comment. `// Take value in range [0, 1]` (line 73) describes deltaDifferenceFraction on line 74, which is in [0,1), not reverseDeltaDifferenceRatio.

No overflow is possible. The ratio is max/min of StrainTimes, with min ≥ 25 ms and max bounded by map length, far below long.MaxValue. The curve is also continuous and periodic at the 0/1 boundary, so the truncation choice cannot change the result.
The doc typos ('returns returns', "it's") are real but a nit. The output-range concern is already handled because Smoothstep clamps internally, so the result stays in [0,1].
Duplicate of ref 3's doc typo, and a nit.

width==0 or negative is unreachable. The sole caller (RhythmEvaluator.cs:76) uses the default width 0.5, and the sibling Smoothstep and Smootherstep helpers do not validate either. This is generic defensive-validation advice.
Variable naming taste in a 3-line helper.
Readability micro-suggestion (the ternary equals width - |x|). Not a defect.
Requests to add focused tests. Test requests are not defects.

Its separate demand to bump OsuDifficultyCalculator.Version is not a defect for a pp-dev PR. pp-dev difficulty changes do not bump Version per PR: #28877 (60eaf088) changed Aim and Speed evaluators on pp-dev without touching it, and 20250306 was set in a master merge (33251275). symfony__symfony@2b9721f.pr_summary: Docblock-only PR on the 7.3 branch. It adds a PHPStan/Psalm array-shape type to the `$content` constructor parameter and to the `getContent()` return type of the Mercure notifier's MercureOptions (src/Symfony/Component/Notifier/Bridge/Mercure/MercureOptions.php). The shape lists the browser Web Notification options: actions, badge, body, data, dir, icon, image, lang, renotify, requireInteraction, silent, tag, timestamp and vibrate. `content` itself was added earlier on the same unreleased 7.3 branch (d54febf32, with tests passing `['tag' => '1234', 'body' => 'TEST']`), and it was meant to carry Notification options. Runtime behaviour does not change: MercureTransport::doSend still json_encodes `$options->getContent()` into the ActivityStreams `content` field as-is. The only real problem is one wrong type in the new shape: `vibrate` is documented as `int[]`, but the API also accepts a single integer.

defects.title: vibrate documented as int[] only; the Notification API VibratePattern also accepts a single integer
defects.statement: The new shape declares `vibrate?: int[]` in both the constructor @param and the getContent() @return. The Web Notification `vibrate` option is a VibratePattern (`unsigned long or sequence<unsigned long>`), so a valid value such as `['vibrate' => 200]` gets flagged by PHPStan/Psalm even though MercureTransport forwards it unchanged to the client and it works. The shape should be `int|list<int>` (or `int|int[]`). This shape is the only contract for the option, and it is the whole deliverable of this PR.
defects.evidence: MercureOptions.php:39 ` *     vibrate?: int[],` (in `@param array{...}|null $content`) and :96 ` *      vibrate?: int[],` (in `@return array{...}|null` of getContent()). MercureTransport.php doSend: `json_encode([... 'content' => $options->getContent(), ])` passes the array through with no normalisation, so the docblock is the only type contract, and the browser Notification API accepts `vibrate: 200` as well as `vibrate: [200, 100, 200]`.
defects.notes: To count, a comment must say that `vibrate` is typed as an int array only, while the Notification/Vibration API (VibratePattern) also accepts a single integer, so the type should be `int|int[]` / `int|list<int>`. Flagging either line 39 or line 96 counts. Near-misses that do NOT count: saying `int[]` should be `list<int>` without mentioning the single-int form; general comments that the shape is too loose or too strict (e.g. `actions?: array` too broad, or the shape rejects custom keys); and remarks about the duplicated shape.

excluded.reason: `actions?: array` is less specific than the Web Notification action shape, but it is not wrong. Tightening it to `list<array{action,title,icon}>` is a precision nicety in a docblock and has no concrete consequence. Trivial.

Asks for a @phpstan-type/@psalm-type alias to remove the duplicated @param/@return shape. Symfony production code does not use such aliases, and repeating a shape across @param and @return is routine there. Its only cost is editing two places, which is a style/maintainability nit a Symfony maintainer would not insist on.

excluded.reason: Same as ref 2: duplicating a shape across @param and @return is conventional in Symfony, and the only concrete cost is a two-place edit. That is not a defect. The indentation difference is a whitespace nit.
Whitespace-only formatting difference: 6-space indentation and ` *  }|null` in the @return block vs 5 spaces in the constructor. A style nit with no consequence.

All three argue that the closed shape narrows an 'existing' arbitrary-array contract, so custom keys like `['orderId' => 123]` would be flagged. It was meant to carry Web Notification options (its tests pass `tag`/`body`), and this PR exists to document exactly that shape, as requested in the linked #60140 review discussion. Runtime behaviour is unchanged, since only static analysis sees the docblock. Whether the payload should be open-ended is a product decision, not a bug the PR introduces.
